venues.name: CC Atlanta
venues.weather: Rainy with highs in the 50s and lows in the 40s. Consistent light rain throughout the evening.
venues.narrative: **CCATL — Wednesday 11/25, Thanksgiving Eve (MOD MKZ // JK; entered by JK; posted 1:04am ET 11/26)** Net $2,239 vs target $1,646 (136.0%). Food $220; no events. Comps $59.35 (2.7%) — F&F $40.65, Industry Love $5.10, manager comp $13, O4W $0.60. 73 guests; check avg $30.67. Thanksgiving Eve started pretty quiet, with a small pop of guests around 5pm, a lull through 6–7pm, and guest flow picking back up at 8pm. The quietest Trivia Night since the program started — which says a lot about how successful trivia has been, since most or all seats are usually filled. Lots of big groups tonight, not surprising with the holiday tomorrow; the team is curious how the holiday weekend will compare with last year given unkind weather across much of the country. Guest flow built gradually into a nice crowd from 8pm to close, including several neighborhood regulars on a cold, rainy night. The opener was cut early and the second closing bartender was cut at 9pm; the closing bartender and barback handled the volume well with MOD support. Kitchen: a slow night for food, with most guests just having drinks. No events. No maintenance needs. Low: Chareau Aloe — out of stock for the past two weeks. No-shows not charged. Highlight: seeing two regulars who have been coming since the soft-opening phase and who turn out to know several other neighborhood regulars.

venues.name: CC Nashville
venues.narrative: **CCNSH — Wednesday 11/25, Thanksgiving Eve (MOD MD, Chef JMS; entered by BC; posted 2:41am ET 11/26)** Net $3,277 vs target $1,227 (267.1%). Food $141; event sales $500. Comps $70.20 (2.1%) — employee discount, bingo credit, Neuhoff employee, Neuhoff resident, industry. 92 guests; check avg $35.62. A fun Thanksgiving-eve Wednesday. A slower start — the parking garage was the emptiest it has been since last holiday season. Trivia began around 7:15pm to give more teams the chance to show; the usual host was out for the holiday and a fill-in hosted. More teams joined throughout the game, most of them first-timers. The managers used the early time to prepare for the weekend. Volume and pace picked up around 9:15pm, and by 9:45pm the room was steady and moving until close. Lots of families and out-of-town friends, many staying for a few hours; a decent crowd was still in when service concluded at midnight. Kitchen: John Michael held it down and was present on the floor. Events: see Morgan for details. 86: ponies, GF buns. Low: Taco Tuesday. No incidents; no-shows not charged. Highlight: a guest and her group celebrating her birthday.

venues.name: D&C Denver
venues.narrative: **DVR — Wednesday 11/25, Thanksgiving Eve (AM MOD Maggie S; PM MOD Maggie H; entered by MJH; posted 2:03am ET 11/26)** Net $10,133.54 vs target $7,677 (132.0%). No events — the event and 'including events' fields were entered as NA, so Total Net Sales and Total Food Sales are used. AM (coffee) $794.75, D&C PM $9,338.79, Garden/6A n/a. Food $1,964.25. Comps $286.55 (2.8%). 253 guests (Tock); check avg $40.05 (net / guests). AM notes: not filled in ('Loading...'). PM: Thanksgiving Eve really popped off — lots of families in together and pretty massive pops in the 5pm, 7pm and 9pm hours, with $2,300 in the 5pm hour alone. No one was cut early; all hands were needed. Kitchen: a pretty steady night, with prep under way for Thanksgiving; a new member joined the morning crew and stayed through the evening to help and try the food. Pass on: prep tomorrow will be pretty decent — the word is service will be for hotel guests only, but prep should still account for potential walk-ins unless told otherwise; only one jar of caviar plus a tiny bit in another container. 911: lime Chantilly, poppyseed vinaigrette, red beet purée, finishing creamed spinach, honey butter quenelle, chicken thigh in brine, ranch dressing. Low: cherry vermouth jam and reduction, coconut gel (out of date), Kopache (five orders), crushed pistachios, burger meat portions, Wagyu flank (count of 10). Watch: pesto at a little under a quart, kiwi ponzu should be started within 48 hours, preserved lemon aioli. Event notes: Thanksgiving family meal at 1:30pm. Break make-up complete. No incidents; no-shows not charged. Highlight: dinner rolls shared with the team.

venues.name: D&C East Village
venues.narrative: **EV — Wednesday 11/25, Thanksgiving Eve (MOD Kyler, Chef Steves; entered by Max K; posted 2:42am ET 11/26)** Net $7,016 vs target $4,648 (150.9%). Food $606, beverage $6,410; no events. Comps $299.16 (4.2%) — a team member's mom came in, plus some finicky DNLs. 182 guests (Sevenrooms); check avg $38. Happy Blackout Wednesday: from 6:30pm on, the night was an absolute blur of pre-holiday craziness. A regular celebrated a birthday at the bar. A small lull between 7:30 and 8pm suggested the night might be chill — it was not. From 8:15pm right up to last call at 12:45am, the door pulled off some inventive seating arrangements to keep the bar as full as possible at all times — a great example of how creativity at the door can yield great results. Big shout-out to the entire team for being adaptable and on top of it. Kitchen: 86 pickles and oysters. Door: 41 degrees with no vestibule. As expected, the night before Thanksgiving brought a wild divergence of groups, from quiet dates to converging friends to multigenerational crews. A lot of parties fluctuated in size during their stay, which made for a high-skill night of deciding when to accommodate and when to truncate; many native New Yorkers return, meet up with school friends and form large groups. An obscene number of table transfers, handled well by the floor. One group let ahead of the line spent more than $200 in an hour. 2 no-shows (7:30pm and 7:45pm two-tops) — badly timed, causing the only fallow period of the night; not yet charged. Menu count 20/20. Glassware breakage: 0.

venues.name: D&C Los Angeles
venues.narrative: **LA — Wednesday 11/25, Thanksgiving Eve (MOD Gigi + Joe; Chef Angel; entered by Joe; posted 7:25am ET 11/26)** Net $11,272 vs target $5,135 (219.5%). Food $2,012; Marquee $8,003; Standing Room $3,269; event sales not reported. Comps $262 (2.3%) — birthday, anniversary, gifts. Guest count & check average was entered as '$278 - $100.65': recorded as 278 guests and a $100.65 check average as reported (net / 278 guests would be about $40.55, so the $100.65 looks like a per-check rather than per-guest figure). Weather was entered as 'No'. A very busy night from start to finish — the first night of the new Fall/Winter cocktail menu, the launch of Season's Greetings, and the first day of the new style of menus. Guests were excited to see the new menu, though a couple asked for the 'normal menu'. The drinks were very well received, with none sent back all night. The room filled up soon after open, right in time to open Season's Greetings at 7pm. Both rooms were full with a nice waitlist around 9pm, and it was non-stop burn and turn all night. Pace of service was great, and many guests asked to sit specifically in Season's Greetings. A great night and a great beginning to a very busy month ahead. Kitchen: busy night, handled very well. Maintenance: water taps. No incidents; no-shows charged. Highlight: seeing the new menus roll out.

venues.name: D&C Washington DC
venues.weather: Cooler with rain later in the evening
venues.narrative: **DC — Wednesday 11/25, Thanksgiving Eve (MOD Marcus; entered by Marcus; posted 1:02am ET 11/26)** Net $4,680.61 incl. events vs target $4,108 (113.9%). Marquee bar $5,163.87; Garden n/a; total sales $5,163.87. Food $526. Comps $95.60 (2.0%) — employee discount 50% $42.50, friends & family 15% $7.20, Industry Love 10% $7.90, service recovery item $38.00. 121 guests (48 walk-ins, 73 reservations); guest check avg $40.70 as reported. D&C: started the night with 57 on the books and the biggest pop planned for 8–8:30pm. Down a set of hands at the bar, the team went to the backup plan: a server trainee switched over to barback, another team member moved to the floor, and the MOD took the door. Early on, a guest arrived with a Resy reservation that did not show in SevenRooms; a couple more Resy bookings missing from SevenRooms were found and added manually, and the team is following up with Resy and Zocha — if a guest says they booked on Resy and can't be found, check with the door. With quite a few cocktails 86'd, the team had fun doing dealer's choice. Lots of familiar faces, neighbors from next door and industry friends in town. Once the rain started things slowed around 11pm, with a natural last call at 11:30pm. The whole team did an incredible job on a busy night. Kitchen: a solid Wednesday; chips and dip, cookies, and bread and butter were the most popular items, and the cook jumped in touching tables and running food. Kitchen close not checked. Went well: adaptability, connection, teamwork. Do better: keep manicuring tables and the bar top; stay proactive about ticket times — watch the KDS and let tables know if food may take a few extra minutes. No incidents; no-shows not charged; no-show revenue $0. Maintenance: curtain, hot water heater. Highlight: seeing the room bumping and all guests smiling.

venues.name: Municipal Grand F&B
venues.narrative: **MG — Wednesday 11/25, Thanksgiving Eve (AM Sam; PM Sam/Eva; entered by Alexis; posted 1:21am ET 11/26)** Net $6,568 vs target $5,066 (129.6%). Morning bar $780, evening bar $3,678, Sun Club $0, Hot Eye $1,298 (parts sum to $5,756 vs $6,568 total net entered). Food $2,222; no events; comps $157 (2.4%). Guests 151 (42 AM + 109 PM OpenTable); check avg $43.50 (net / guests). Note: the morning guest count (42), morning sales ($780) and morning notes are identical to Monday 11/23's report, so the morning fields may have been carried over. Morning (as entered): a very quiet daytime with almost no hotel guests; one food tour; cut as needed. Evening: also quiet; guests were well attended to and pleased with both beverages and food; an early night for the team. Sun Club: closed. Hot Eye: a really slow start with just a couple of guests, then by 9:30pm the room did a 180, with large groups of college kids and some local industry packing it out for a couple of hours; it died back down around 11pm and was empty by midnight. Kitchen: slow night, good ticket times, no complaints or send-backs; only low item is steaks (12 count), no 86s. No incidents. Highlight: Happy Thanksgiving Eve.

venues.name: D&C Seattle
venues.weather: Rainy and windy all day! Walk-ins definitely were a smaller portion of our guests tonight, could have been because of the weather (likely the holiday)
venues.narrative: **SEA — Wednesday 11/25, Thanksgiving Eve (MOD Frank; entered by Frank; posted 3:26am ET 11/26)** Net $7,815 vs target $7,995 (97.7%). Food $900; no events. Comps $608.16 (7.7% as reported) — mostly a larger service recovery, an employee discount and a bill comp for a VIP, plus a few DNLs, community members/investors and a couple of F&F discounts. 176 guests; avg guest spend $49.09 as reported. An eventful night despite the heavy rain and the holiday. Walk-ins weren't as heavy as usual, but the books were pretty full, especially between 6:00 and 7:30pm; the door made it work and everyone was seated quickly for their reservations. Large parties and VIPs were the story of the night, along with parties who rescheduled tomorrow's reservations to today. The room stayed pretty full until close, most likely because the rain caused guests to linger — and they kept spending, for a strong guest average. Everyone got a break in and the team supported each other well. Kitchen: a pretty mellow night, but still beat its target for the day; staff meal was fantastic. No events. No maintenance needs. Low: Heart of Stone sour (sub incoming). No incidents; no-shows not charged. Highlight: hosting VIP family guests and walking them to their dinner reservation.
